source.title: Mirror, Mirror on the Wall: Prompt Echoing in Small Instruct Language Models
source.authors: Inez Okulska; B. Naskrȩcki; Jan Piotrowski; Tomasz Steifer

page_placements.theme: Induction-like heads in degenerate repetition and prompt echo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether ablating heads selected by a prefix-matching score reduces prompt copying, a different behavioral test from the original induction-head and in-context-learning measurements.
record.gate_note: Experiment 4 measures prompt-echo outcomes after ablating copying-score heads and random heads; its separately reported model and ablation-condition results are recorded below. Experiment 2 reports training-data overlap for echoing and non-echoing prompts, recorded as findings not covered by the listed versions. Table 1 measures echo rates but does not measure induction heads, and Table 2 deliberately seeds copying by forcing prompt tokens; neither is a qualifying result for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Olsson et al. prefix-matching score as a tool to pick heads, then measures only prompt-echo rates in instruct LLMs after ablating them. It never reports the heads' prefix-matching scores, so it does not show whether induction heads exist in each model (V4). It also does not test previous-token composition or the [A][B]…[A]→[B] algorithm in attention-only models (V1). It does not touch training dynamics or in-context learning (V2, V3, V5–V7). The ablation result concerns a related but different construct, the causal role of copy-score heads in echoing, so it belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that echoing is influenced by memorization but not fully explained by it, and once started is driven by internal copying mechanisms. The abstract states it more strongly: echoing is 'primarily driven by the model's induction heads'. The heads are identified only by prefix-matching score and are not otherwise verified as induction heads; the authors call head ablation a coarse intervention.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a prefix-matching score to select heads and ablates them during prompt-echo generation. It does not reproduce the original induction-head formation or in-context-learning measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Echo outcomes differ by model and by the number/type of heads ablated; the authors report larger decreases for top-16 than top-8 candidate heads and larger decreases for candidate-head ablation than random-head ablation across models.

fits_no_version.finding: In six small instruct models, ablating the top 8 or 16 heads by prefix-matching score cut prompt-echo rates to near zero. Ablating 16 random heads reduced them much less, e.g. Gemma 4.97% to 4.65%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heads with high prefix-matching scores causally contribute to spontaneous prompt echoing in instruct LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Echo-generating prompts more often matched the first 5 words of a training document than non-echoing prompts: OLMo 32.63% vs 9.38%, SmolLM 26.33% vs 17.97%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Echo-prone prompts overlap partially with public instruction-tuning data, though the authors call the criterion weak.

record.problems: The study is limited to small instruct models and a narrow prefix-based prompt-echo measure. The authors state that head ablation is coarse and does not identify the full circuit. The training-data overlap analysis covers only two model families and uses a weak first-5-words match criterion. Table 3 reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying Table 3 or Experiment 2 results were omitted. Table 1 echo rates were not recorded because they do not measure induction-head behavior; Table 2 was excluded because copying was deliberately initiated by forced prompt tokens.

untested.parts: All: no attention-only models, no previous-token-head composition, no [A][B]…[A]→[B] test, and no prefix-matching scores reported.
All: in-context learning is not measured.
All: heads are ranked by prefix-matching score, but scores are not reported, so induction-head presence per model is not shown.
All: training data and setup are not varied.
All: few-shot task learning is not measured.
All: formation stages are not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1/V4 'supports' labels are removed. The rows measure echo suppression by copy-score heads, not induction-head mechanism or prevalence. Table 2 (forced echo) is rightly excluded because it induces copying deliberately. No version verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether induction heads form by composing with an earlier previous-token head, or whether they implement the canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] task. It tests the causal role of heads selected by a prefix-matching score in prompt echoing.
Training trajectories, abrupt formation, in-context-learning gains, and a training-loss bump are not measured.
The study does not measure in-context learning or the proportion of it carried by induction heads.
The study tests selected small instruct models from six model families, not multiple training runs, other architectures or modalities, or broad universality across sizes.
The study does not vary training data or training setup to test induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Few-shot task learning and alternative mechanisms for it are not measured.
The study does not measure the stages or timing of induction-head formation.

relation.reason: Induction-head scoring supplies an intervention tool; the reported outcomes concern prompt echoing rather than a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study uses prefix-matching scores to select heads and measures prompt-echo reduction after ablation. It does not measure formation, in-context learning, or head prevalence required by the listed versions.

source_check.notes: Echo rates concern diagnostic prompt distributions, not deployment prevalence. The authors acknowledge that head ablation does not fully identify the underlying circuit.
